cells.tense: The testing is happening in the open now, and the answer is coming back real.
cells.ask: Name one step already under way that you intend to keep taking, and tell yourself what it is for.
cells.core:
The checking has moved out of the head and into what you actually do. A stretch of road is visible, and there is enough nerve to use it — so the next stretch gets taken and the verdict forms from contact rather than from planning. That is the thing working.

Keep it going with one deliberate move. Name a step already being taken, and say, to yourself, what it is for. That gives the next stretch something to hold, and it keeps the testing honest, because a commitment that gets walked keeps getting answered. Nothing here asks for the full route. What is in front of you is enough to walk.
cells.sheetLine: You test the commitment by walking it, not by waiting for the road.
cells.verb: testing the commitment by walking it
cells.place: a road lit only as far as the next step

cells.tense: Ahead of you the verdict keeps getting rehearsed before anything has been tried.
cells.ask: Write down the one step you would take if the whole road could not be seen, and take it today.
cells.core:
There is a way of doing this where half the road is dark and it does not matter — the next stretch gets taken on the information at hand, and the rest shows up later. That works because the step is small enough to survive being wrong.

What is happening instead is that the outcome gets run before the attempt. The script is written, the failure played out in advance, and the fine-tuning happens in the head instead of on the road. The way through is smaller than certainty: pick the next real step, write it down, and take it today. One step will not settle anything, and it does not need to.
cells.sheetLine: You're rehearsing the verdict instead of taking the next step.
cells.verb: testing the commitment by walking it

cells.tense: You stood in the doorway a while back and never told anyone what you meant to say.
cells.ask: Take one next step on something you care about, and let one person you trust see it.
cells.core:
Walking this in pieces is how it goes when it is going well — a step, a small correction, another step — and the next bit of road shows up behind the one just taken. No destination is needed. Just enough light for the next move, and the willingness to make it.

What stopped is the walking. Some earlier point made stepping forward feel unsafe, and it has been standing still since. Nothing about the path changed.

You do not need the whole route back. One next step is enough, and doing it in front of a person you trust puts ground back under it. In front of someone who will not ask for the plan, a commitment gets its first move back.
cells.sheetLine: The road is still there. It's the walking that hasn't restarted.
cells.verb: testing the commitment by walking it
cells.place: a road lit only as far as the next step

cells.tense: You are already committing to this in how you spend your days, and calling it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Say once, to one person, that a practice you keep up is what your days rest on.
cells.core:
A commitment that works does not need a speech. It needs to be known, at least to the one keeping it — and what keeps getting returned to, the practice kept up under the name of errands, is already doing that work.

What is missing is only the saying. Nobody can name what it means from the outside; you can, and you have not. So say it once. One sentence to one person is enough. The work is already happening, and the credit belongs to you. Naming it costs little and returns the account of these days to where it started.
cells.sheetLine: The commitment is already in your days. The saying of it isn't.
